recognize_zh: Factor VIII-related antigen（vWF）免疫染色把巨核細胞染成深棕色，可見其大小落差很大：除少數大型細胞（右下、中央）外，散布大量只比周圍造血細胞略大的單核小型巨核細胞（micromegakaryocytes），這種小而單核的型態即巨核細胞發育不良的線索。
features: IHC for factor VIII-related antigen (von Willebrand factor) with strong brown cytoplasmic staining of megakaryocytes
Megakaryocytes markedly variable in size; numerous small mononuclear or hypolobated forms comparable to surrounding precursors
Few large megakaryocytes (lower right, center) with hypolobated nuclei
Megakaryocytes scattered singly and in loose small groups rather than tight clusters
Faint background staining of plasma/endothelium; negative hematopoietic background with interspersed adipocytes
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for factor VIII-related antigen (von Willebrand factor) on the bone marrow core biopsy highlights megakaryocytes with strong cytoplasmic staining. The megakaryocytes show a wide range in size, including numerous small mononuclear forms (micromegakaryocytes) and a few larger hypolobated cells, distributed singly and in small loose groups. Nonspecific faint staining of background plasma and stroma is present. Increased small mononuclear megakaryocytes are a feature of megakaryocytic dysplasia; in the setting of GATA2 deficiency with monosomy 7, findings are consistent with refractory cytopenia of childhood.

ddx.vs: Normal marrow megakaryocytes are predominantly large with multilobated nuclei, with only rare small immature forms, unlike the many micromegakaryocytes highlighted here.
CML dwarf megakaryocytes occur in a markedly hypercellular granulocytic marrow with BCR::ABL1, not in a hypocellular pediatric marrow with monosomy 7.
AMKL shows sheets or clusters of megakaryoblasts with blast-level immaturity and >=20% blasts, whereas here the small megakaryocytes are scattered with no blast increase.
